Upādānagocchaka (The Group on Clinging)
Section on Analysis:
Root Condition.
Dependent upon a phenomenon that is an object of clinging, a phenomenon that is an object of clinging arises by way of the root condition—dependent upon the clinging to views.
Grasping at sensual pleasures; dependent on grasping at sensual pleasures, grasping at views; dependent on grasping at rules and observances, grasping at sensual pleasures;

dependent on grasping at sensual pleasures, grasping at rules and observances; dependent on grasping at a doctrine of self, grasping at sensual pleasures; dependent on grasping at sensual pleasures, grasping at a doctrine of self.

Dependent on a state that is clinging (*upādāna*), a state that is not clinging arises by way of the root condition (*hetupaccaya*): dependent on the clingings, the associated aggregates and mind-produced matter arise.
Dependent on a state that is clinging, states that are both clinging and not clinging arise by way of the root condition:

dependent on the clinging to views (*diṭṭhupādāna*), the clinging to sensual pleasures (*kāmupādāna*) arises, along with the associated aggregates and mind-produced matter; [dependent on] the clinging to sensual pleasures...
… [all the wheel should be completed] … Conditioned by a state that is not associated with clinging, a state that is not associated with clinging arises by way of root condition:
conditioned by one aggregate not associated with clinging, three aggregates and mind-produced matter arise … two aggregates … [and so on] … at the moment of rebirth-linking.
Dependent on one aggregate not associated with clinging, there arise three aggregates and kamma-produced matter; ... two aggregates ...
dependent on aggregates, there arises the physical basis; dependent on the physical basis, there arise aggregates; dependent on one great primary ...
dependent on great primaries, there arise mind-originated matter, kamma-produced matter, and derived matter.
Dependent on a state that is not grasping, a state that is grasping arises by way of root condition: dependent on aggregates that are not grasping, the [corresponding] graspings arise.
Dependent on a state that is not grasping, states that are both grasping and not grasping arise by way of root condition:
dependent on one aggregate that is not grasping, three aggregates, the graspings, and mind-produced matter arise … [and so on] … dependent on two aggregates … [and so on].
Dependent on [clinging], two aggregates and clinging-born matter arise.

Dependent on a state that is both clinging and non-clinging, a state that is clinging arises by way of root condition: dependent on view-clinging and its associated aggregates, sense-desire clinging arises. (All wheels should be performed.
Dependent on a state that is both clinging and non-clinging, a state that is non-clinging arises by way of root condition: [dependent on] non-clinging...

Dependent on one aggregate that is clinging and [one] great primary element, there arise three aggregates and mind-produced matter … and so on … dependent on two aggregates … and so on … dependent on clinging and the great primary elements, there arises mind-produced matter.
Dependent on a state that is both clinging and not-clinging, states that are both clinging and not-clinging arise.

Conditioned by root-cause: dependent on one aggregate that is not a clinging, and view-clinging, there arise three aggregates, sense-desire clinging, and mind-produced matter; [dependent on] two aggregates … (The cycle should be constructed.
Object-condition.

Dependent on a state that is an object of clinging (*upādāna*), a state that is an object of clinging arises by way of object-condition (*ārammaṇa-paccaya*). (Nine questions are to be formulated; matter is to be excluded.
Section on Enumeration:
Pure.
In the cause condition, nine; in the object condition, nine; in the predominance condition, nine (nine in all cases); in the resultant condition, one …pe… in the non-disappearance condition, nine.
2.11.1.1.2. Negative Exposition: Section on Analysis (Paccayapaccanīya Vibhaṅgavāra).
Dependent on a state that is neither a cause nor grasping, a state that is neither a cause nor grasping arises by way of the non-cause condition:
dependent on one rootless aggregate that is neither a cause nor grasping, three aggregates and mind-produced matter arise … [and so on] … dependent on two aggregates … [and so on] …
At the moment of rootless rebirth-linking ... depending on the aggregates there is the [heart-]base; depending on the base there are the aggregates; one great primary ...
depending on the great primaries there is mind-produced matter, kamma-produced matter, and derived matter;
external ... nutriment-produced ... temperature-produced ... of non-percipient beings ... associated with doubt.
In dependence on aggregates accompanied by restlessness, arises delusion accompanied by doubt and accompanied by restlessness.
Regarding the condition "not-object":
In dependence on a state that is a clinging (upādāna), a state that is not-clinging arises by way of the not-object condition—namely, mind-produced matter in dependence on the clingings.
Dependent on a state that is not associated with clinging (*noupādāna*), a state that is not associated with clinging arises by way of the object-condition (*ārammaṇapaccaya*):

dependent on aggregates not associated with clinging, mind-originated matter (*cittasamuṭṭhāna-rūpa*) arises; at the moment of rebirth-linking (*paṭisandhi*), dependent on aggregates not associated with clinging, kamma-produced matter (*kaṭattā-rūpa*) arises;
dependent on the aggregates, the physical basis (*vatthu*) arises; one great primary element (*mahābhūta*) … [and so on] … up to the non-percipient beings (*asaññasatta*).
Dependent on states that are both with-clinging and without-clinging, a state without-clinging arises by way of the object condition:
dependent on clinging and its associated aggregates, mind-produced matter arises; dependent on clinging and the great primary elements, mind-produced matter arises.
Not by way of predominance condition ... not by way of proximity condition ... pe ... not by way of strong-dependence condition. Not by way of prenascence condition:

dependent on a state that is clinging, a state that is clinging arises by way of prenascence condition—namely, in the formless realm, dependent on the clinging to a doctrine of self, the clinging to sensual pleasures arises; dependent on the clinging to sensual pleasures, the clinging to a doctrine of self arises.
Dependent on a state that is an object of clinging (*upādāna*), a state that is not an object of clinging arises by way of non-prenascence condition:
in the formless realm, dependent on clinging, the associated aggregates arise; dependent on clinging, mind-originated matter arises. (Abbreviated;
there are nine questions regarding the two types of clinging in the formless realm.)
In the Enumeration Chapter, under the Pure [Combinations]:
one for not-root, three for not-object, nine for not-predominance, three for not-proximity …pe… [and so on] … none for not-strong-dependence.
Three; nine in not-prenascence, nine in not-postnascence, nine in not-repetition, three in not-kamma, nine in not-resultant,
one in not-nutriment, one in not-faculty, one in not-jhāna, one in not-path, three in not-association,
nine in not-dissociation, three in not-absence, three in not-disappearance.

2.11.1.3.1–4. Positive Conditionality, etc.

Conditioned by a state that is clinging, a state that is clinging arises by way of root-condition: conditioned by the clinging to views, the clinging to sensual pleasures [arises]... three [factors]. (The same as in the Paṭicca-vibhaṅga.)
Conditioned by a state that is not derived from clinging (*anupādāna*), a state that is not derived from clinging arises by way of root-condition (*hetu-paccaya*):

conditioned by one aggregate that is not derived from clinging, three aggregates and mind-produced matter arise … two aggregates … [and so on] … at the moment of rebirth-linking … conditioned by the aggregates,
the [heart-]base arises … [down to] the internal great elements … conditioned by the [heart-]base, aggregates that are not derived from clinging arise.

Conditioned by a state that is not grasping, a state that is grasping arises by way of root condition: conditioned by aggregates that are not grasping, the graspings arise; conditioned by the [heart-]base, the graspings arise.

conditioned by one aggregate that is not grasping, three aggregates, the graspings, and mind-produced matter arise … [and so on] … conditioned by two aggregates … [and so on] …
...pe... conditioned by the [heart-]base, clinging arises; conditioned by the great elements, mind-originated matter arises;
conditioned by the [heart-]base, clinging and the associated aggregates arise.
Conditioned by a state that is both clinging and non-clinging, a state that is clinging arises by way of root condition: namely, view-clinging.

With the associated aggregates as condition, there is clinging to sensual pleasures; and with clinging to sensual pleasures and the associated aggregates as condition, there is clinging to views (the cycle should be constructed).
With clinging to views and the [internal] base as condition, there is clinging to sensual pleasures (the cycle should be constructed).
With a state that is both clinging and non-clinging as condition, a state that is non-clinging arises by way of root-condition: the non-clinging...

Conditioned by one aggregate that is clinging and the [corresponding] great primary elements, there arise three aggregates and mind-produced matter … pe … conditioned by two aggregates … pe … (the cycle should be constructed). Conditioned by clinging and the great primary elements, there arises mind-produced matter;
conditioned by clinging and the [heart-]base, there arise the aggregates that are not clinging.
Conditioned by states that are both grasping and not-grasping, there arise states that are both grasping and not-grasping by way of root condition:
conditioned by one non-grasping aggregate and the grasping of views, there arise three aggregates, the grasping of sensual desire,
and mind-produced matter … (the cycle continues) … conditioned by the grasping of views and the [heart-]base, there arises the grasping of sensual desire.
And the associated aggregates … [cycle] … By way of object condition … (In the section on object condition not rooted in clinging, the five bases and the physical basis should be included.
Nine in root, nine in object, nine in predominance (nine in all cases), one in result … [etc. … nine in non-disappearance.
Positive (Anuloma).
Conditioned by a state that is not associated with clinging (*noupādāna*), a state not associated with clinging arises by way of the root-cause condition (*nahetupaccaya*):
conditioned by one rootless (*ahetuka*) aggregate not associated with clinging …pe… at the moment of rootless rebirth-linking (*paṭisandhi*) …pe… (up to the non-percipient beings) the eye-base.
Conditioned by [the respective bases], eye-consciousness arises …pe… conditioned by the body-base, body-consciousness arises;

conditioned by the [heart-]base, rootless aggregates not associated with clinging arise; and conditioned by doubt-accompanied or restlessness-accompanied aggregates and the [heart-]base, doubt-accompanied or restlessness-accompanied delusion arises.

By way of not-root: one; by way of not-object: three; by way of not-predominance: nine; by way of not-proximity: three; by way of not-contiguity: three ... pe ... by way of not-prenascence: nine ... pe ... by way of not-kamma: three; by way of not-resultant: nine (the same as in the Paṭicca [Dependent] Chapter) ... pe ... by way of not-disappearance: three. [There are] nine in the case of the cause, nine in the case of the object, nine in the case of the predominance [condition] (nine in all cases), one in the case of resultant, ... pe ... nine in the case of disappearance, nine in the case of non-disappearance.

2.11.1.7.1. Positive Order of Conditions (Paccayānuloma):
Analysis Section (Vibhaṅgavāra) – Root Condition (Hetu)
A state that is clinging is a condition for a state that is clinging by way of the root-cause condition (*hetupaccaya*).
The roots that are clingings are a condition for the associated clingings by way of the root-cause condition. (The basic formula should be stated here.

[They are] a condition for the clingings by way of root-condition. (The root-text should be composed.

Roots that are both clinging and non-clinging are a condition, by way of root-condition, for associated aggregates and for mind-produced matter.

The aggregates and the states of clinging are related to mind-produced matter by way of the root-condition.
Object Condition:

A state that is a state of clinging is related to a state that is a state of clinging by way of the object-condition. Taking the states of clinging as an object, states of clinging arise... [three] (these should be formulated using "taking as an object").
A state that is not an object-of-clinging is a condition, by way of object-condition, for a state that is not an object-of-clinging:
having given a gift, [practiced] virtue …pe… or performed the duty of observance, one reviews it, relishes it, and delights in it;
taking that as an object, lust arises, wrong view arises; doubt …pe… restlessness …pe… or grief arises.
Formerly practiced [wholesome states] ... [as above] ... Having emerged from jhāna, one reviews the jhāna; noble ones, having emerged from the path, review the path;

they review the fruit ... [as above] ... they review Nibbāna. Nibbāna is a condition, by way of object-condition (ārammaṇa-paccaya), for change-of-lineage (gotrabhū), purification (vodāna), the path, the fruit, and adverting (āvajjanā). Noble ones, in the case of non-clinging (noupādāna) ... [as above] ... [Nibbāna is a condition by way of object-condition].
They review defilements that have been abandoned … [and so on] … they review defilements that have been suppressed;
they review former habitual practices … [and so on] … the eye … [and so on] … the physical basis, and the aggregates not associated with clinging, as impermanent … [and so on] … sorrow arises;

one sees a form with the divine eye, hears a sound with the divine ear-element; by means of the knowledge of penetration of minds, one [knows] one possessing a mind not associated with clinging … [and so on].
It knows the mind; the base of infinite space [is the object] of the base of infinite consciousness... the base of nothingness [is the object] of the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception...
the visible-form base [is the object] of eye-consciousness... the tangible-object base [is the object] of body-consciousness...

the aggregates not derived from clinging [are the objects] of the knowledge of the modes of psychic power, the knowledge of penetration into others' minds, the knowledge of recollection of past lives, and the knowledge of passing away and rebirth according to one's kamma.
Knowledge of the future is related to adverting by way of object-condition.
A state not associated with clinging is related to a state associated with clinging by way of object-condition:
having performed an act of giving … morality … or the observance-day rites, one relishes and delights in them; taking that as object, lust arises, or wrong view [arises].

arises; formerly well-performed deeds … [as above] … jhānas … [as above] … the eye … [as above] … one relishes and delights in the aggregates that are not objects of clinging with respect to the physical basis (*vatthu*);
taking that as an object, lust arises, wrong view arises.
A state that is not an object of clinging is a condition, by way of object-condition, for a state that is both an object of clinging and not an object of clinging: [as in the case of] giving.
...pe... having performed virtuous conduct (*sīla*) ...pe... having performed the observance-day rite (*uposathakamma*) ...pe... having performed deeds well-done in the past ...pe...

having emerged from meditative absorption (*jhāna*), one relishes and delights in the absorption ...pe... the eye ...pe... the physical basis (*vatthu*); [thereby] one relishes and delights in the aggregates that are not associated with clinging (*anupādāna*).
Taking that as an object, clinging and the associated aggregates arise.
States that are both clinging and non-clinging are related to a state that is clinging by way of the object condition ... three. (To be elaborated by taking [the states] as the starting point.
Predominance:

A state that is clinging is related to a state that is clinging by way of the predominance condition. Object-predominance: By esteeming clinging, clingings arise ... three. (These are only object-predominance.)

A state that is not an object-of-clinging is a condition for a state that is not an object-of-clinging by way of predominance-condition (*adhipatipaccaya*): as object-predominance (*ārammaṇādhipati*) and as co-nascent predominance (*sahajātādhipati*).

As object-predominance: having given a gift, [having undertaken] virtue … pe … the observance-duty (*uposathakamma*) … pe … [recalling] the past … pe … having emerged from a jhāna, one esteems, reviews, enjoys, and delights in that jhāna; or the Noble Ones [do so].
Having emerged from the path, they esteem and review the path ... [as above] ... the fruit is a condition for the path by way of predominance-condition (*adhipatipaccaya*);
the eye ... [as above] ... the physical basis (*vatthu*) and the aggregates not associated with clinging (*noupādāna-khandha*), one esteems, relishes, and delights in them;
esteeming that, lust arises, wrong view arises. Conascent predominance: predominance not associated with clinging (*noupādānādhipati*).
It is a condition for its associated aggregates and for mind-produced matter by way of predominance-condition (*adhipatipaccaya*).

A state that is not of the nature of clinging (*anupādāna*) is a condition for a state that is of the nature of clinging by way of predominance-condition—namely, object-predominance (*ārammaṇādhipati*) and conascence-predominance (*sahajātādhipati*).
Object-predominance: having performed an act of giving ... morality ... or the observance-day duty (*uposathakamma*), one esteems it...
Having made [it] an object, one relishes it and delights in it; esteeming that, lust arises and wrong view arises.

Regarding the past... pe... regarding the jhānas... pe... regarding the eye... pe... regarding the physical basis (vatthu) and the aggregates not associated with clinging (anupādāna-khandha), one esteems them, relishes them, and delights in them;
esteeming those, lust arises and wrong view arises. Co-nascent predominance (sahajātādhipati): predominance not associated with clinging (anupādānādhipati).

as object-predominance and as conascence-predominance. Object-predominance: [thinking] "Giving... morality... the observance-day rite... [previously performed]"... *etc.*
... pe ... jhāna ... pe ... eye ... pe ... [taking] the bases (vatthu) and the aggregates not associated with clinging as an object of esteem, one relishes and delights in them;

predominance not associated with clinging is a condition, by way of predominance-condition, for the associated aggregates, for the clingings, and for mind-produced matter.

preceding non-grasping aggregates are a condition for succeeding graspings and for the associated aggregates.

preceding instances of clinging and their associated aggregates are a condition by way of proximity-condition for succeeding instances of clinging.
